primary: Nuclear reactor availability losses and subsequent regional wholesale electricity prices
backups: Mississippi water levels and barge freight pressure
FAA capacity advisories and airline cancellation spillovers
alternatives_considered: MSHA mine withdrawal orders and subsequent mine production
PTAB adverse patent decisions and competitor exposure
EPA facility enforcement and customer/supplier disruption
NLRB election outcomes and labor-cost exposure
selection_reason: A direct operational scarcity mechanism, original daily administrative observations, a small physical outcome dataset and existing nearest-neighbor research. The merit-order mechanism is known; novelty, delayed equity response and underexploitation are unproved.
evidence_target: Level A reconstructed descriptive association only; no historical actionability or executable profitability claim
selection_of_dates: Two three-day calendar blocks fixed before retrieval; all reactor rows retained. No famous outage or observed price selected. Exact routes must be evidenced by publisher indexes.
outcome_source_probe: At most one small 2023 EIA/ICE annual electricity workbook and corresponding gas workbook, inspect schemas and first three source-order PJM/TETCO observations only. No signal-outcome join or effect calculation.
pass_for_proposal: Actual source rows, consistent unit/date fields, a usable outcome schema and a manageable proposed sample; historical publication/revision limitations may be retained at Level A. Missing exact historical public versions alone does not fail Level A.
stop: Any denied route stops its requests; no bypass or automatic backup. A decisive primary limitation ends the source check. Full sample, joins, event counts, statistical estimates and returns require subsequent owner approval.
